# Finding $\limsup_{j\to\infty}|a_j|^{1/j}$

## Interpreting the Sequence

The problem defines $a_j = \frac{(1+1/j)^{2j}}{e^j}$. (The summation notation in the problem appears to be a notational artifact; the sequence is the $j$-th term.)

## Computing $|a_j|^{1/j}$

Since $a_j > 0$ for all $j$, I can work directly:

$$|a_j|^{1/j} = \left(\frac{(1+1/j)^{2j}}{e^j}\right)^{1/j} = \frac{(1+1/j)^{2j\cdot(1/j)}}{e^{j\cdot(1/j)}} = \frac{(1+1/j)^2}{e}$$

## Taking the Limit

Now I evaluate the limit as $j \to \infty$:

$$\lim_{j\to\infty}|a_j|^{1/j} = \lim_{j\to\infty}\frac{(1+1/j)^2}{e} = \frac{\bigl(\lim_{j\to\infty}(1+1/j)^2\bigr)}{e} = \frac{1^2}{e} = \frac{1}{e}$$

Since the limit exists (not just the limsup), the $\limsup$ equals the ordinary limit.

## Result

$$\limsup_{j\to\infty}|a_j|^{1/j} = \boxed{\dfrac{1}{e}}$$
